export class ClaimInviteDto {

      'Hex-encoded ECIES descriptor ref for read access re-wrapped for the recipient ' +

  @IsString()

Now I fully understand: the invite carries `writeDescriptorRef` (sharer decides write authority at invite creation); the claimer re-wraps and submits `dto.writeDescriptorRef`. The claim must store the claimer's re-wrapped value **only if the invite granted write** (`invite.writeDescriptorRef !== null`) — otherwise a read-only invite yields a write grant. 224	  private async upsertIpnsRecord(
225	    userId: string,
226	    ipnsName: string,
227	    metadataCid: string,
228	    signedRecord: Uint8Array,
229	    _publicKey?: Uint8Array,
230	    encryptedIpnsPrivateKey?: string,
231	    keyEpoch?: number,
232	    expectedSequenceNumber?: string,
233	    generation?: string
234	  ): Promise<IpnsRecord> {
235	    // The cache is keyed by ipnsName alone — there is one canonical row per name.
236	    // The caller's authority to update it was already proven by signature
237	    // verification in publishRecord (key possession), so no ownership/share check
238	    // is needed here: whoever holds the key updates the canonical record.
239	    const existing = await this.ipnsRecordRepository.findOne({ where: { ipnsName } });
240	
241	    // Anti-rollback: the incoming record's EMBEDDED sequence (covered by the
242	    // signature, so tamper-evident) must not regress below the stored record's.
243	    // Without this, anyone who observes the public IPNS record could replay an
244	    // old-but-still-valid signed copy (no key needed) to roll the canonical row
245	    // back to a stale CID — independent of the optional expectedSequenceNumber CAS.
246	    // Equal sequences are allowed (idempotent re-publish of the current record).
247	    // incomingParsed is set here when existing?.signedRecord is present (anti-rollback
248	    // path) so S1 can reuse it below without a second parseIpnsRecord call.
249	    let incomingParsed: { value: string; sequence: bigint } | null = null;
250	    if (existing?.signedRecord) {
251	      const [incoming, stored] = await Promise.all([
252	        parseIpnsRecord(signedRecord),
253	        parseIpnsRecord(existing.signedRecord),
254	      ]);
255	      if (incoming.sequence < stored.sequence) {
256	        throw new ConflictException({
257	          statusCode: 409,
258	          message: 'IPNS record sequence regression rejected (rollback/replay)',
259	          currentSequenceNumber: existing.sequenceNumber,
260	        });
261	      }
262	      incomingParsed = incoming;
263	    }

> **Resolved by PR #541** (merged 2026-06-22). Verified already-fixed in the 2026-06-23 pending-todo audit (independent adversarial re-check confirmed). Archived from pending.

## Problem

The IN-04 "accepted circular-dependency" comments in `ipfs.module.ts`,
`vault.module.ts`, and `pending-unpin.module.ts` give a factually-wrong
rationale. They claim a shared module providing `IPFS_PROVIDER` would create a
circular dependency, so each module self-provides the factory instead.

That is not true. The `IPFS_PROVIDER` factory depends only on `ConfigService`
(a leaf — `ConfigModule` imports nothing from these modules). A standalone:

```ts
@Module({
  imports: [ConfigModule],
  providers: [IPFS_PROVIDER],
  exports: [IPFS_PROVIDER],
})
class IpfsProviderModule {}

It also carries an `is_root` boolean\n(`isRoot`). Nothing at the DB level prevents two rows with the same `user_id`\nboth having `is_root = true`, so a user could in principle accumulate multiple\n\"root\" records and make root lookups ambiguous.\n\nToday the invariant is upheld at the application layer: a user's root IPNS name\nis deterministically derived from their root folder key (one root per user), and\nthe publish/resolve plane keys by `ipnsName` alone — so this is a\ndefense-in-depth gap, not an observed bug.\n\n## Proposed fix\n\nAdd a partial unique index and back it with a migration:\n\n```ts\n// entity\n@Index('UQ_ipns_records_user_root', ['userId'], {\n  unique: true,\n  where: '\"is_root\" = true',\n})\n```\n\n```sql\n-- migration\nCREATE UNIQUE INDEX \"UQ_ipns_records_user_root\"\n  ON \"ipns_records\" (\"user_id\") WHERE \"is_root\" = true;\n```\n\n## Before doing this\n\nConfirm the one-root-per-user invariant actually holds for every flow that sets\n`is_root = true` (vault creation, import/export, any future multi-vault work).\nIf multi-root per user is ever intended, this constraint must NOT be added.\nA fresh forward migration is required — the Phase 66 cutover migration has\nalready shipped; do not edit it in place.\n"

The\n`@Unique(['ipnsName'])` constraint guarantees exactly one wins — the loser gets a\nPostgres unique-violation, which currently surfaces as a 500 rather than the\nclean `409` the TEE-04 contract promises for \"concurrent publishes → exactly one\n409, zero lost updates.\"\n\nNo data is lost (the constraint is authoritative); only the rejected racer's\nHTTP status is wrong. The existing publish-gate suite (Test 16) exercises\nconcurrent *forward* publishes against an existing row, not concurrent *first*\npublishes.\n\n## Proposed fix\n\nWrap the first-publish `save` and translate the unique violation to a\n`ConflictException` (409), mirroring the CAS `affected === 0` path:\n\n```ts\ntry {\n  const saved = await this.ipnsRecordRepository.save(folder);\n  ...\n} catch (e) {\n  if (e instanceof QueryFailedError && /* unique_violation 23505 */) {\n    throw new ConflictException({ statusCode: 409, message: 'IPNS record already exists' });\n  }\n  throw e;\n}\n```\n\nAdd an sdk-e2e case: two concurrent first-publishes of a fresh name → exactly\none 200 + one 409.\n"
}

=== check-api-client.sh ===
#!/bin/bash

# Check if API source files are staged but generated client files are not
# This prevents forgetting to run `pnpm api:generate` after API changes

# Files that indicate API changes requiring client regeneration
API_PATTERNS=(
  "apps/api/src/.*\.dto\.ts"
  "apps/api/src/.*\.controller\.ts"
  "apps/api/src/.*\.entity\.ts"
)

# Generated files that should be updated when API changes
GENERATED_FILES=(
  "packages/api-client/openapi.json"
)

# Get staged files
STAGED_FILES=$(git diff --cached --name-only)

# Check if any API source files are staged
API_CHANGED=false
for pattern in "${API_PATTERNS[@]}"; do
  if echo "$STAGED_FILES" | grep -qE "$pattern"; then
    API_CHANGED=true
    break
  fi
done

if [ "$API_CHANGED" = false ]; then
  exit 0
fi

# API files changed - check if generated files are also staged
# Only flag files that have actual uncommitted changes (not already up to date)
MISSING_GENERATED=()
for file in "${GENERATED_FILES[@]}"; do
  if ! echo "$STAGED_FILES" | grep -q "^${file}$"; then
    # Only require staging if the file actually has unstaged changes
    if git diff --quiet "$file" 2>/dev/null; then
      continue  # File is up to date, no staging needed
    fi
    MISSING_GENERATED+=("$file")
  fi
done

if [ ${#MISSING_GENERATED[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "⚠️  API source files changed but generated client files are not staged!"
  echo ""
  echo "You modified API DTOs, controllers, or entities but didn't regenerate the client."
  echo ""
  echo "Run this command and stage the changes:"
  echo ""
  echo "    pnpm api:generate"
  echo ""
  echo "Missing generated files:"
  for file in "${MISSING_GENERATED[@]}"; do
    echo "    - $file"
  done
```

  "content": "## Phase 66 — API schema cutover, IPNS publish gate, and tombstone\n\nCuts the API over to the `node/v3` schema and makes the IPNS publish/resolve plane integrity-authoritative.\n\n### What changed\n\n**IPNS publish/resolve integrity plane**\n- Publish is now a single **atomic conditional UPDATE** that fuses the sequence CAS (`sequence_number = :expected`), the forward-only `generation` gate, and the tombstone gate (`tombstoned_at IS NULL`) — `affected === 0` drives a 409/410 disambiguation. No TOCTOU, no lost updates (TEE-04, TEE-07).\n- `parseCachedRecord` is a 3-way union: a null-`signedRecord` shared-folder row applies a **seq floor** (network record served only at/above floor, else fail closed); a CID mismatch fails closed (TEE-05).\n- **Tombstone** state machine: `POST /ipns/tombstone` (owner-only), publish + resolve return `410 IPNS_TOMBSTONED`, EOL renewal blocked by the same `tombstoned_at IS NULL` predicate, and the name is unenrolled from TEE republishing (WRITE-04).\n\n**Schema cutover (greenfield drop-recreate migration)**\n- `folder_ipns` → `ipns_records` (`IpnsRecord`); `public_key` column dropped — the Ed25519 pubkey is always recovered from the k51 name via `publicKeyFromIpnsName` (DATA-03).\n- `share_keys` table/entity deleted; `shares` slimmed to one descriptor-ref grant row per recipient (`readDescriptorRef`/`writeDescriptorRef`); revoke is a hard DELETE (DATA-01, DATA-02).\n- sdk-core publish primitives thread an optional `generation` so the server gate is provable end-to-end; web share/invite consumers are intentionally compile-gate stubbed for Phase 68.\n- Regenerated `@cipherbox/api-client`.\n\n### Ship-review gates\n\n| Gate | Result |\n|------|--------|\n| Verify (UAT) | PASS — all 6 success criteria verified |\n| Secure | SECURED — 17/17 threats closed (T-66-E1 found OPEN and remediated, see below) |\n| Validate (Nyquist) | VALIDATION_PLACEHOLDER |\n| SDK E2E | GREEN — ipns-publish-gate 5/5; rotation/read/write suites pass; 89 pre-existing `D-01` quarantine skips unchanged |\n| IPNS unit | 174/174 pass |\n| CodeRabbit CLI | 15 findings triaged (2 fixed, 3 deferred to todos, rest false-positive/already-handled) |\n\n### Fixes applied during ship review\n\n- **T-66-E1 (security, high):** the invite claim path minted a write grant from `dto.writeDescriptorRef` without checking the invite — a read-only invite could yield write authority. Write authority is now presence-derived from `invite.writeDescriptorRef`.\n- Rate-limit the new `POST /ipns/tombstone` endpoint (`@Throttle`, matching siblings).\n- Tighten `rootIpnsName` validation on the share/invite DTOs to the canonical CIDv1 libp2p-key pattern.\n- `psql execSync` timeout in the publish-gate e2e helpers.\n- Removed dead `UpdateEncryptedKeyDto`, `shares/types.ts`, and the unused `_publicKey` publish param left by the cutover.\n- Added a focused `share-invite.service.spec.ts` restoring claim-path security coverage (T-66-E1, self-claim, root-identity, idempotency).\n\n### Deferred (todos under `.planning/todos/pending/`)\n\n- `ipns_records` per-user root partial unique index (CodeRabbit F2 — needs an invariant decision + new migration).\n- First-publish INSERT race → clean `409` instead of unique-violation `500` (CodeRabbit F13 — correctness already guaranteed by the unique constraint).\n- `share_invites.claim_count` CHECK constraint (CodeRabbit F11 — app already enforces the bound).\n- Restore full shares-module unit coverage beyond the claim path (the cutover deleted 5 specs; only the security-critical slice was restored here).\n\n### Accepted risks\n\n- Migration is greenfield drop-recreate, `down()` throws (D-01 — staging wiped on deploy, no prod data).\n- Web share/invite throw-stubs are intentional; Phase 68 wires the real path before any web ship.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\n"
}

{

  "old_string": "  async tombstoneRecord(userId: string, ipnsName: string): Promise<void> {\n    await this.ipnsRecordRepository\n      .createQueryBuilder()\n      .update(IpnsRecord)\n      .set({ tombstonedAt: new Date() })\n      .where('ipns_name = :ipnsName AND tombstoned_at IS NULL AND user_id = :userId', {\n        ipnsName,\n        userId,\n      })\n      .execute();\n    // Unenroll from TEE republish schedule regardless of whether the UPDATE matched\n    // (idempotent: if already unenrolled, unenrollIpns returns 0 affected).\n    await this.republishService.unenrollIpns(userId, ipnsName);\n  }",
  "new_string": "  async tombstoneRecord(userId: string, ipnsName: string): Promise<void> {\n    const result = await this.ipnsRecordRepository\n      .createQueryBuilder()\n      .update(IpnsRecord)\n      .set({ tombstonedAt: new Date() })\n      .where('ipns_name = :ipnsName AND tombstoned_at IS NULL AND user_id = :userId', {\n        ipnsName,\n        userId,\n      })\n      .execute();\n\n    if (result.affected === 0) {\n      // affected === 0 is ambiguous: the row is either already tombstoned\n      // (idempotent success) or it does not exist / is not owned by the caller.\n      // Distinguish with an owner-scoped lookup so a mistyped or unowned name\n      // returns 404 instead of a misleading 200; an already-tombstoned row is a\n      // no-op success.\n      const owned = await this.ipnsRecordRepository.findOne({ where: { ipnsName, userId } });\n      if (!owned) {\n        throw new NotFoundException(`IPNS record not found: ${ipnsName}`);\n      }\n    }\n\n    // Unenroll from TEE republish schedule regardless of whether the UPDATE matched\n    // (idempotent: if already unenrolled, unenrollIpns returns 0 affected).\n    await this.republishService.unenrollIpns(userId, ipnsName);\n  }"
}

<h3>Greptile Summary</h3>

This PR delivers Phase 66's three-part schema cutover: replaces `folder_ipns` with `ipns_records` (adding `tombstoned_at` and `generation` columns), slims `shares` to a single descriptor-ref grant per recipient with hard-delete revocation, and makes the IPNS publish plane integrity-authoritative through an atomic conditional UPDATE that fuses sequence CAS, forward-only generation gate, and tombstone gate in one SQL statement.

- **IPNS publish gate**: `upsertIpnsRecord` is now a single atomic UPDATE with fused `sequence_number = :expected AND generation <= CAST(:incoming AS bigint) AND tombstoned_at IS NULL`; `affected === 0` drives a follow-up read to disambiguate 409 vs 410, eliminating TOCTOU and lost updates (TEE-04/07).
- **Tombstone state machine**: `POST /ipns/tombstone` (owner-only, rate-limited) sets `tombstoned_at` and unenrolls from TEE republishing; publish and resolve both check the field and return 410 GONE. The `tombstoneRecord` follow-up read correctly distinguishes 404 (not found/unowned) from idempotent no-op (already tombstoned).
- **Share schema cutover**: `share_keys` table deleted; `shares` reduced to one `readDescriptorRef`/`writeDescriptorRef` row per recipient; T-66-E1 fix gates write authority from `invite.writeDescriptorRef` (not claimer-supplied DTO input); `syncIpnsRecordSequence` in republish now guards `tombstonedAt: IsNull()` closing the TEE race window.

<h3>Confidence Score: 4/5</h3>

The atomic publish gate, tombstone state machine, and share schema cutover are all well-implemented; one gap exists in the batch publish path where a tombstoned record silently returns a generic failure with no way for the client to distinguish it from a transient error.

The batch publish path absorbs the 410 GONE from the tombstone gate and emits `{ success: false, sequenceNumber: '0' }` — identical to a transient network failure — with no `errorCode` or escalation. A client retry loop or TEE rotation batch will keep re-attempting a permanently retired name indefinitely. The individual publish endpoint correctly surfaces 410; this gap is specific to the batch path and was introduced by this PR adding tombstone support.

   A client retry loop (SDK rotation, batch background sync) receives the same shape for a permanently retired name as for a transient network error and will keep retrying indefinitely, burning rate-limit quota against a name that can never publish again. The individual `POST /ipns/publish` endpoint correctly surfaces 410; the batch path is the only gap introduced by this PR.

   The least-invasive fix mirrors the `ConflictException` treatment — re-throw the 410 `HttpException` to fail the whole batch, consistent with the existing comment "if any record has a conflict, fail the entire batch". Alternatively, surface a `reason` / `errorCode` field in the per-record result DTO so callers can distinguish permanent from transient failures.

No `NODE_ENV` gating — the publish is a detached/fire-and-forget promise (line 131). The strong hypothesis: under the full e2e suite's load, the delegated-routing PUT gets rate-limited and dropped after retries in CI (the "Rate limited ... retrying in 5000ms" path), so the network record never lands — no CI-passing test actually requires the network record, Test 15 is the first. The robust fix is to make Test 15's network record **deterministic** (seed it directly into mock-ipns-routing, the same philosophy as its psql DB seeding) instead of depending on the unreliable detached publish. 1	/**
2	 * Mock Delegated Routing Service for E2E Testing
3	 *
4	 * Implements the IPFS delegated routing API for IPNS records:
5	 * - PUT /routing/v1/ipns/{name} - Store an IPNS record
6	 * - GET /routing/v1/ipns/{name} - Retrieve an IPNS record
7	 *
8	 * Records are stored in-memory and reset when the service restarts.
9	 * This allows E2E tests to run without polluting the public IPFS DHT
10	 * and avoids sequence number conflicts from repeated test runs.
11	 */
12	
13	import Fastify from 'fastify';
14	
15	const fastify = Fastify({
16	  logger: {
17	    level: process.env.LOG_LEVEL ?? 'info',
18	    transport:
19	      process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'
20	        ? { target: 'pino-pretty', options: { colorize: true } }
21	        : undefined,
22	  },
23	});
24	
25	// CORS headers for browser-based recovery tool testing (read-only access)
26	fastify.addHook('onRequest', async (request, reply) => {
27	  reply.header('Access-Control-Allow-Origin', '*');
28	  reply.header('Access-Control-Allow-Methods', 'GET, OPTIONS');
29	  reply.header('Access-Control-Allow-Headers', 'Content-Type, Accept');
30	  if (request.method === 'OPTIONS') {
31	    return reply.status(204).send();
32	  }
33	});
34	
35	// In-memory storage for IPNS records
36	// Key: IPNS name (k51... or bafzaa...), Value: raw record bytes
37	const ipnsRecords = new Map<string, Buffer>();
38	
39	// Health check endpoint
40	fastify.get('/health', async () => {
41	  return { status: 'ok', records: ipnsRecords.size };
42	});
43	
44	// GET /routing/v1/ipns/{name} - Retrieve IPNS record
45	fastify.get<{ Params: { name: string } }>('/routing/v1/ipns/:name', async (request, reply) => {
46	  const { name } = request.params;
47	
48	  const record = ipnsRecords.get(name);
49	  if (!record) {
50	    return reply.status(404).send({
51	      error: 'record not found',
52	      name,
53	    });
54	  }
55	
56	  fastify.log.info({ name, size: record.length }, 'Retrieved IPNS record');
57	
58	  return reply.status(200).header('Content-Type', 'application/vnd.ipfs.ipns-record').send(record);
59	});
60	
61	// PUT /routing/v1/ipns/{name} - Store IPNS record
62	fastify.put<{ Params: { name: string } }>('/routing/v1/ipns/:name', async (request, reply) => {
63	  const { name } = request.params;
64	
65	  // Get raw body as Buffer
66	  const body = request.body as Buffer;
67	  if (!body || body.length === 0) {
68	    return reply.status(400).send({
69	      error: 'empty request body',
70	    });
71	  }
72	
73	  // Store the record (overwrites any existing record)
74	  // Note: We intentionally don't validate sequence numbers here.
75	  // This allows tests to reset state by simply restarting the service.
76	  ipnsRecords.set(name, body);
77	
78	  fastify.log.info(
79	    { name, size: body.length, totalRecords: ipnsRecords.size },
80	    'Stored IPNS record'
81	  );
82	
83	  return reply.status(200).send({ ok: true });
84	});
85	
86	// Configure to accept raw binary bodies
87	fastify.addContentTypeParser(
88	  'application/vnd.ipfs.ipns-record',
89	  { parseAs: 'buffer' },
90	  async (_request: unknown, payload: Buffer) => payload

> AGENT

The throttle setup: a `BypassableThrottlerGuard` skips throttling only when `THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET` is set on the API **and** the request carries the bypass header. Critically, the CI workflow sets `THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET` only on the *test step*, not the *API process* — so in CI the bypass silently fails and throttling is enforced. Under the heavy suite, Test 15's many resolves get 429'd and the SDK returns null → "expected null not to be null". Your fix is exactly right: disable API rate limits in the test env. Let me read the guard + module to implement a clean blanket test-env disable.

1	import { Injectable, ExecutionContext } from '@nestjs/common';
2	import { ThrottlerGuard } from '@nestjs/throttler';
3	import { timingSafeEqual } from 'node:crypto';
4	
5	/**
6	 * Extends ThrottlerGuard with a bypass header for test environments.
7	 *
8	 * When THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET is set, NODE_ENV is not 'production', and
9	 * a request includes a matching X-Throttle-Bypass header, rate limiting
10	 * is skipped. This allows SDK E2E and load tests to run against staging
11	 * without hitting 429s.
12	 *
13	 * Security:
14	 *   - Production always enforces rate limits (NODE_ENV check)
15	 *   - If the env var is unset/empty, the header is ignored entirely
16	 *   - Uses crypto.timingSafeEqual to prevent timing attacks
17	 */
18	@Injectable()
19	export class BypassableThrottlerGuard extends ThrottlerGuard {
20	  async canActivate(context: ExecutionContext): Promise<boolean> {
21	    const secret = process.env.THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET;
22	
23	    if (secret && process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production') {
24	      const request = context.switchToHttp().getRequest();
25	      const rawHeader = request.headers['x-throttle-bypass'];
26	      const header = Array.isArray(rawHeader) ? rawHeader[0] : rawHeader;
27	      if (header && safeEqual(header, secret)) {
28	        return true;
29	      }
30	    }
31	
32	    return super.canActivate(context);
33	  }
34	}
35	
36	/** Constant-time string comparison using Node.js crypto. */
37	function safeEqual(a: string, b: string): boolean {
38	  const bufA = Buffer.from(a);
39	  const bufB = Buffer.from(b);
40	  if (bufA.length !== bufB.length) return false;
41	  return timingSafeEqual(bufA, bufB);
42	}

Now it's clear. The per-route `@Throttle` decorators (e.g. resolve = 30/min) override the test-relaxed global config, and the default throttler tracker is **per-IP** — so in CI all localhost traffic shares one bucket. The heavy suite exhausts it, resolves get 429'd, the SDK returns null, and Test 15's at-floor assertion fails. Locally it passes only because the bypass header works (secret is in local `.env`). Your fix is right — disable throttling in the test env at the guard (covers both global and per-route `@Throttle`). Implementing:

The monitor's spawn uses `stdio: 'ignore'` and only fires at critical context, so it's not the source. The real clue: in settings.local.json the PostToolUse `gsd-context-monitor.js` command uses a **relative** path (`.claude/hooks/...`), unlike the other hooks which use `"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/.claude/hooks/...`. If the hook runs with a CWD other than repo root, node can't find the script → `cjs/loader:1433`. Let me confirm:

> AGENT

**Confirmed.** Running the hook from a non-root CWD reproduces it exactly: `Cannot find module '/private/tmp/.claude/hooks/gsd-context-monitor.js'`. 

Root cause: in `.claude/settings.local.json`, the PostToolUse `gsd-context-monitor.js` (and SessionStart `gsd-check-update.js`) hook commands use a **relative** path (`.claude/hooks/...`), unlike the other GSD hooks which use `"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/.claude/hooks/...`. Since many of my Bash commands `cd` into subdirs (`cd apps/api && …`), the PostToolUse hook resolves the relative path from that subdir, can't find the script, and node throws `cjs/loader:1433`. It's non-blocking (the tool still runs), just noise — but it fires on every `cd`-ing command. Let me fix it by making those two paths absolute, matching the other hooks.

> AGENT

I've addressed all three of your points. Summary:

**1. SDK E2E failure (Test 15) — root-caused and fixed properly**
You were right on both counts. I reverted the publish-bypass approach. The real cause: the `BypassableThrottlerGuard`'s default tracker is **per-IP**, so the full E2E suite hammering the API from one localhost IP shares a single bucket and exhausts the per-route `@Throttle` limits (resolve = 30/min). Those 429s made the SDK return `null`, so Test 15's at-floor serve saw "null" — and only Test 15 hits it because it's the one test forced onto the network path. The header-bypass was silently failing in CI because the workflow set `THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET` only on the test step, not the API process. Per your direction, I disabled rate limiting outright when `NODE_ENV=test` (commit `e48a0cdc9`). **Validated locally**: ran the full E2E suite in `NODE_ENV=test` with **no** bypass secret — Test 15 passed in 318ms, 11/11 green. Staging still uses the header; production unaffected.

**2. CI Test failure (separate issue, already green)** — the cutover deleted the shares specs but left their jest coverage thresholds. Restored real coverage (shares.service + 3 controllers + ipns.controller); `Test`, `Typecheck`, `Build`, `Lint`, `CodeRabbit` all passed on the prior run.

**3. The `cjs/loader:1433` hook errors** — diagnosed: in `.claude/settings.local.json`, the PostToolUse `gsd-context-monitor.js` and SessionStart `gsd-check-update.js` hooks used a **relative** path (`.claude/hooks/...`) while every other GSD hook uses `"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/.claude/hooks/...`. Whenever a Bash command `cd`s into a subdir (which I do constantly: `cd apps/api && …`), the hook resolves the relative path from that subdir, can't find the script, and node throws. Non-blocking noise. Fixed both to absolute paths (local-only file, gitignored) — should stop now.

Also pushed the greptile **outside-diff P1** fix: `publishBatch` was masking the tombstone `410` as a generic per-record failure, so a retry loop would hammer a retired name forever — now it re-throws the 410 to fail the batch (commit `8348e1fa0`, with a regression test).

CI is re-running on `e48a0cdc9`; I'll report once it settles and re-sweep for any new CodeRabbit/greptile threads.

The `&` + blind `sleep 2` masks the crash, so it's silently never run. Test 15's at-floor serve is the first/only test that resolves via the network delegated-routing path, so it's the only one that fails. It passes locally because the mock server is actually up there.

> AGENT

The fix is pushed and CI is re-running. Since this PR branch lives in the same repo, the updated `ci.yml` takes effect on this run.

**Root cause (the real one):** The SDK E2E job started the mock delegated-routing server with `node dist/server.js`, but the entry compiles to `dist/index.js`. Node crashed instantly, and `&` + `sleep 2` swallowed the error — so the routing server has **never run in CI** since PR #318. Test 15 (seqFloor at-floor serve) is the only test that resolves through the delegated-routing network path, so it's the only one that failed (null resolve). It passed locally because the mock server is actually up there. The Dockerfile and `desktop-e2e.yml` both already use `dist/index.js` — only this one job had the typo.

Fix: corrected the entry to `dist/index.js` and replaced the blind sleep with a `/health` poll that fails the job loudly, so a dead mock server can't silently regress again. The throttle fix you directed stays — it's correct and prevents a separate flake class.

Background poll `bapb4r8ho` is watching the SDK E2E job; I'll report when it settles.

Critical finding from reading the code: **fix [5] (idempotent same-seq CID guard) breaks test [19]**. The renewal test currently signs `seq=2n` with a *different* CID at the same DB sequence — which, once [5] rejects same-seq-different-CID with a 400, would no longer return the asserted 409. CodeRabbit's [19] suggestion (replay `seq=1n`) is exactly what makes them consistent: `seq=1 < dbSeq 2` hits the anti-rollback gate → 409. So [5] and [19] are coupled and I'll own both, then re-run the e2e suite to confirm.

+// Signed 64-bit upper bound of the bigint "generation" column.
+const BIGINT_MAX = 9223372036854775807n;
+
+@ValidatorConstraint({ name: 'isNonNegativeBigInt', async: false })
+class IsNonNegativeBigIntConstraint implements ValidatorConstraintInterface {
+  validate(value: unknown): boolean {
+    if (typeof value !== 'string') return false;
+    try {
+      const parsed = BigInt(value);
+      return parsed >= 0n && parsed <= BIGINT_MAX;
+    } catch {
+      return false;
+    }
+  }

import { ApiProperty } from '@nestjs/swagger';
import { IsString, Matches, MaxLength } from 'class-validator';

export class GetInvitesForItemQueryDto {
  @ApiProperty({
    description: 'IPNS name (k51...) of the root shared node',
  })
  @IsString()
  // Canonical CIDv1 libp2p-key validator (matches CreateInviteDto / ipns resolve/tombstone DTOs):
  // k51qzi5uqu5... (base36 PeerID-style) or bafzaa... (base32 IPNS key CID).
  @Matches(/^(k51qzi5uqu5[a-z0-9]{40,60}|bafzaa[a-z2-7]{50,70})$/, {
    message: 'rootIpnsName must be a valid CIDv1 libp2p-key (k51qzi5uqu5... or bafzaa...)',
  })
  @MaxLength(255)
  rootIpnsName!: string;
}

---
created: 2026-06-30T00:00:00.000Z
title: Add a partial unique index on ipns_records(user_id) WHERE is_root for defense-in-depth
area: data-integrity
severity: low
files:
  - apps/api/src/ipns/entities/ipns-record.entity.ts
  - apps/api/src/migrations/1750000000000-ApiSchemaCutover.ts
---

> Deferred from the Phase 66 ship (CodeRabbit major finding F2). Out of the
> phase's publish-gate/cutover domain and requires a data-model invariant
> decision + a migration, so it is not a low-risk in-scope fix.

## Problem

`IpnsRecord` (`@Entity('ipns_records')`) enforces uniqueness only on
`ipnsName` (`@Unique(['ipnsName'])`). It also carries an `is_root` boolean
(`isRoot`). Nothing at the DB level prevents two rows with the same `user_id`
both having `is_root = true`, so a user could in principle accumulate multiple
"root" records and make root lookups ambiguous.

Today the invariant is upheld at the application layer: a user's root IPNS name
is deterministically derived from their root folder key (one root per user), and
the publish/resolve plane keys by `ipnsName` alone — so this is a
defense-in-depth gap, not an observed bug.

## Proposed fix

Add a partial unique index and back it with a migration:

```ts
// entity
@Index('UQ_ipns_records_user_root', ['userId'], {
  unique: true,
  where: '"is_root" = true',
})
```

```sql
-- migration
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "UQ_ipns_records_user_root"
  ON "ipns_records" ("user_id") WHERE "is_root" = true;
```

## Before doing this

Confirm the one-root-per-user invariant actually holds for every flow that sets
`is_root = true` (vault creation, import/export, any future multi-vault work).
If multi-root per user is ever intended, this constraint must NOT be added.
A fresh forward migration is required — the Phase 66 cutover migration has
already shipped; do not edit it in place.
```

  "content": "---\ncreated: 2026-06-30T00:00:00.000Z\ntitle: Decide whether a same-sequence IPNS republish may change the CID (D-09 idempotent path)\narea: data-integrity\nseverity: medium\nfiles:\n  - apps/api/src/ipns/ipns.service.ts\n  - apps/api/src/ipns/ipns.service.spec.ts\n---\n\n> Deferred from the Phase 66 ship (CodeRabbit major finding, ipns.service.ts:351).\n> This targets the PRE-EXISTING D-09 / Pitfall 4 idempotent-republish behavior\n> (plan 58-02), which is outside Phase 66's publish-gate/tombstone domain and is\n> deliberately exercised by an existing test, so reversing it is a risky design\n> change rather than a low-risk in-scope fix.\n\n## Problem\n\nIn `upsertIpnsRecord`, when the incoming record's embedded sequence equals the\nstored `sequence_number` the publish is treated as an idempotent republish:\nthe row is NOT advanced, but `latestCid` and `signedRecord` ARE overwritten with\nthe incoming values. CodeRabbit's concern: a validly-signed record for the SAME\nsequence but a DIFFERENT CID can mutate the authoritative `latestCid` without\nadvancing the sequence (an equivocation/fork).\n\nThe current behavior is intentional today: the test\n`allows idempotent republish (embedded = DB seq) without incrementing DB sequenceNumber`\n(ipns.service.spec.ts ~2022) publishes a NEW CID at the same sequence and asserts\n`latestCid` is updated — labelled \"latestCid must be updated even on idempotent\nre-sign (Pitfall 4)\". So this is a documented decision, not an oversight.\n\n## Decision required\n\nClarify the intended TEE 6-hour re-sign semantics (D-09 / Pitfall 4):\n\n- If the TEE only ever re-signs the SAME content to refresh validity/EOL, then a\n  same-sequence publish with a different CID is illegitimate and should be\n  rejected with 400 (CodeRabbit's proposal). The idempotent test must then change\n  to re-sign the SAME CID, and the renewal e2e test already replays seq=1 (Phase\n  66 change), so it is unaffected.\n- If a same-sequence re-sign is allowed to point at refreshed metadata by design,\n  document WHY overwriting `latestCid` without advancing the sequence is safe\n  (and that resolvers will not observe two divergent values for one sequence).\n\n## Proposed fix (only if \"reject\" is chosen)\n\n```ts\nif (embeddedSeq === dbSeq) {\n  if (metadataCid !== existing.latestCid) {\n    throw new BadRequestException(\n      `Idempotent republish must preserve CID for sequence ${dbSeq}`\n    );\n  }\n  isIdempotentRepublish = true;\n}\n```\n\nDo NOT apply blindly — confirm the TEE re-sign flow first, as it may legitimately\nre-point the CID at the same sequence.\n"
}

  "content": "---\ncreated: 2026-06-30T00:00:00.000Z\ntitle: Validate sharer owns the root before issuing a share invite\narea: security\nseverity: medium\nfiles:\n  - apps/api/src/shares/share-invite.service.ts\n---\n\n> Deferred from the Phase 66 ship (CodeRabbit major finding, share-invite.service.ts:42).\n> CodeRabbit itself tags this a \"Heavy lift\": it needs an ownership source-of-truth\n> decision (which table proves a user owns rootIpnsName/rootNodeId) plus a\n> cross-check, so it is not a low-risk in-scope fix.\n\n## Problem\n\n`createInvite` copies `rootIpnsName` and `rootNodeId` straight from the client\nDTO into the persisted invite for `sharerId`, with no check that the sharer\nactually owns that root or that the `rootIpnsName`/`rootNodeId` pair is\nconsistent. A spoofed invite (root the sharer does not own, or a mismatched\nname/node pair) is later copied verbatim into the `Share` row during claim\n(`share-invite.service.ts` mints the Share from invite fields — T-66-S1).\n\nThe claim path is already hardened against claimer-side spoofing (root identity\nis sourced from the invite, write authority is presence-derived — T-66-E1), but\nthe INVITE-issuance side trusts the sharer's input unconditionally.\n\n## Proposed fix\n\nBefore persisting the invite, verify ownership and pair-consistency:\n\n- Look up the sharer's root (e.g. `ipns_records` / `folder_ipns` row for\n  `userId = sharerId` with `ipnsName = rootIpnsName`, or the vault root) and\n  confirm it exists and is owned by `sharerId`.\n- Confirm `rootNodeId` corresponds to that same root (define the node→root\n  mapping that proves the pair).\n- Reject with 403/400 on mismatch before save.\n\n## Before doing this\n\nDecide the authoritative ownership lookup for a \"root\" (vault entity vs\nipns_records.isRoot vs folder tree). This determines whether the check is a\nsingle indexed lookup or needs a new query path.\n"
}

  "content": "---\ncreated: 2026-06-30T00:00:00.000Z\ntitle: Apply (or explicitly reject) a later invite's grant when a share already exists\narea: data-integrity\nseverity: low\nfiles:\n  - apps/api/src/shares/share-invite.service.ts\n---\n\n> Deferred from the Phase 66 ship (CodeRabbit major finding, share-invite.service.ts:184).\n> Current behavior fails SAFE (it never escalates access), and changing it needs a\n> share-upgrade/merge semantics decision, so it is a deliberate design question\n> rather than a low-risk in-scope fix.\n\n## Problem\n\nIn `claimInvite`, when a `Share` already exists for the (sharer, recipient,\nrootNodeId) triple, the invite is marked claimed and the method returns the\nexisting `shareId` WITHOUT applying the new invite's `readDescriptorRef`,\noptional `writeDescriptorRef`, or `rootGeneration`. So a recipient who first\naccepted a read-only invite and later claims a write (or newer-generation)\ninvite \"succeeds\" but keeps their stale read-only access.\n\nThis fails safe today — the recipient ends up with LESS access than the new\ninvite grants, never more, so it is not an escalation vulnerability — but the\nwrite/generation upgrade is silently dropped, which is surprising.\n\n## Proposed fix (decision required)\n\nPick one:\n\n1. **Upgrade-merge:** when the existing share is found, update its\n   `readDescriptorRef` / `writeDescriptorRef` / `rootGeneration` from the new\n   (validated) invite before returning. Must preserve the T-66-E1 invariant:\n   write authority is presence-derived from the INVITE\n   (`invite.writeDescriptorRef !== null`), never from claimer input. Only ever\n   widen access from a legitimately-issued invite; never let a read-only invite\n   downgrade/clobber an existing write grant.\n2. **Reject:** if the new invite's grant differs from the existing share, throw a\n   conflict BEFORE consuming the invite, and require an explicit re-share /\n   rotation flow to change access.\n\nAdd unit coverage for read→write re-claim and generation-bump re-claim.\n"
}

CI is fully green on `c27669e43` (only Greptile re-review pending). Now your question — and your instinct is right; the direct DB access is a smell worth examining.

## What Test 15 actually tests

It tests one thing: the **resolve endpoint's "seqFloor" gate** for *shared-folder rows that have a sequence number but no `signed_record`*.

Such rows are real. Per the codec (`ipns-record.codec.ts`): a row with a `latestCid`/`sequence_number` but `signed_record = NULL` is "typical of shared-folder rows that were inserted by the sharing protocol and never had a signedRecord written." The recipient of a shared folder knows the sequence *floor* the owner is at, but doesn't hold the signing key, so the API has a floor with no signed bytes. `parseCachedRecord` turns that into a `SeqFloor` discriminant, and the resolve gate (`ipns.service.ts:662`) enforces:

- network record present and `networkSeq >= floor` → **serve it**
- network record below the floor, or absent → **fail closed (null → 404)** — never serve a network record ungated when a floor is known (prevents serving a rolled-back record).

## Step by step

**Part A — null `signedRecord` + floor gating:**
1. `psqlQueryOne` reads Alice's `user_id` (needed to scope the seeded rows).
2. Fresh keypair → `ipnsName`; upload blob → `cid`; publish at seq=1 via the SDK. This writes **both** the DB row (with signed bytes) **and** the network record at seq=1.
3. `psqlExec`: `signed_record = NULL, sequence_number = 100`. Now the row is a `SeqFloor` of 100, network is at 1.
4. Resolve → `1 < 100` → **fail closed → null**. ✓
5. `psqlExec`: `sequence_number = 1` (= network seq).
6. Resolve (with the propagation poll) → `1 >= 1` → **serves**, cid matches. ✓

**Part B — unparseable cached record, no network fallback:**
7. Fresh keypair never published to the network → `ipnsName2`.
8. `psqlExec`: `INSERT` a row with garbage `signed_record` (`\x01020304`) + a stub `latestCid`.
9. Resolve → network has nothing; cached parse throws → **null (404)**, no ungated fallthrough. ✓

## Is the psql necessary? No — not for the logic.

The precondition (null/garbage `signed_record` at a chosen floor) is an **internal DB state you cannot reach through the publish API** — every real publish writes a valid `signed_record`. So you have only two ways to set it up: seed the DB directly (what it does), or drive the entire multi-account shared-folder protocol that produces such rows.

But the gate is **pure decision logic** (compare two integers, type-narrow a union), and it's **already unit-tested** in `ipns.service.spec.ts` — the at-floor serve (`:1067`), the null-signedRecord-no-network → null (`:916`, `:2251`), and the parse-error → null cases all mock the repo + delegated routing and assert exactly these outcomes. So Test 15 is largely re-proving at great cost what unit tests already prove:

- it needs the full live stack,
- it pokes the DB directly (white-box — couples the test to the physical schema/columns),
- and the at-floor case forced the fire-and-forget propagation **poll** — the precise flakiness that cost the earlier CI cycles.

By contrast, Tests 16/17/TEE-07/20 *genuinely* need the live stack: they exercise real concurrency, the publish CAS round-trip, and the tombstone path end-to-end. **Test 15 is the outlier.**

My recommendation: move the below-floor / at-floor / malformed assertions to unit tests (most already exist — you'd add at most the explicit below-floor numeric case) and drop the psql seeding + live-stack dependency from Test 15. If you want to keep *one* e2e that proves the real `/ipns/resolve` endpoint is wired to the gate, the faithful version drives the actual sharing flow to create the null-`signedRecord` row rather than seeding it — but that's heavier and couples to the share stack, so I wouldn't; the unit tests are the right home.

Want me to do that refactor (lift Test 15's cases into the codec/service unit specs and remove the psql helpers), or leave it as-is for this PR and capture it as a follow-up todo?

20	 *   networkSeq < seqFloor   →  fail closed (return null → 404)

28	/**
29	 * Parse an IPNS record to extract CID and sequence number.
30	 * Backed by the `ipns` package via @cipherbox/crypto (parseIpnsRecord).
31	 */
32	export async function parseIpnsRecordBytes(
33	  recordBytes: Uint8Array,
34	  logger: Logger
35	): Promise<IpnsRecordFields> {
36	  try {
37	    const record = await parseIpnsRecord(recordBytes);
38	
39	    // Extract CID from the Value field (format: /ipfs/<cid>)
40	    const valuePath = record.value;
41	    const cidMatch = valuePath.match(/\/ipfs\/([a-zA-Z0-9]+)/);
42	    if (!cidMatch) {
43	      logger.error('Failed to extract CID from IPNS record value');
44	      throw new HttpException('Invalid IPNS record format', HttpStatus.BAD_GATEWAY);
45	    }
46	
47	    const cid = cidMatch[1];
48	    const sequenceNumber = String(record.sequence ?? 0n);
49	
50	    // Base64-encode signature fields if present
51	    const signatureV2 = record.signatureV2
52	      ? Buffer.from(record.signatureV2).toString('base64')
53	      : undefined;
54	    const data = record.data ? Buffer.from(record.data).toString('base64') : undefined;
55	    const pubKey = record.pubKey ? Buffer.from(record.pubKey).toString('base64') : undefined;
56	
57	    logger.debug(`Parsed IPNS record: cid=${cid}, sequenceNumber=${sequenceNumber}`);
58	    return { cid, sequenceNumber, signatureV2, data, pubKey };
59	  } catch (error) {
60	    if (error instanceof HttpException) {
61	      throw error;
62	    }
63	    logger.error(`Failed to parse IPNS record: ${error}`);
64	    throw new HttpException('Invalid IPNS record format', HttpStatus.BAD_GATEWAY);
65	  }
66	}
67	
68	/**
69	 * Parse a cached IpnsRecord row into a verifiable fields bundle.
70	 *
71	 * Returns a three-way discriminated union:
72	 *   - IpnsRecordFields: full fields available (normal row with signedRecord)
73	 *   - SeqFloor: shared-folder row (signedRecord is null, but latestCid exists)
74	 *               → caller must gate network record against the floor sequence
75	 *   - null: no latestCid, or CID mismatch, or malformed name → fail closed (→ 404)
76	 */
77	export async function parseCachedRecord(
78	  cached: IpnsRecord | null,
79	  logger: Logger
80	): Promise<IpnsRecordFields | SeqFloor | null> {
81	  if (!cached?.latestCid) {
82	    return null;
83	  }
84	
85	  // TEE-05 / §6.5 case-split: null signedRecord on a row with a known latestCid is
86	  // expected for shared-folder rows (they are inserted by the sharing protocol and
87	  // never have a signedRecord). Return a seq floor so the caller can gate network
88	  // content without falling through unconditionally.
89	  if (!cached.signedRecord) {
90	    return { seqFloor: cached.sequenceNumber };
91	  }
92	
93	  try {
94	    const parsed = await parseIpnsRecordBytes(cached.signedRecord, logger);
95	    // D-06 (Plan 60-05): discard on CID or sequence mismatch between the signed
96	    // record bytes and the DB columns — a mismatch means the row is inconsistent
97	    // and must not be served.  Warn and return null; the caller will 404.
98	    if (parsed.cid !== cached.latestCid) {
99	      logger.warn(
100	        `Cached signed record CID mismatch for ${cached.ipnsName}: signedRecord=${parsed.cid}, latestCid=${cached.latestCid} — discarding cached result`
101	      );
102	      return null;
103	    }
104	    // DB columns are authoritative for sequenceNumber (upsertIpnsRecord always
105	    // increments it, while the embedded bytes reflect the client's pre-increment value).
106	    //
107	    // D-03: public_key column dropped — publicKeyFromIpnsName is the sole recovery path.
108	    // For Ed25519 the k51... name encodes the public key, so it is the AUTHORITATIVE
109	    // source and is always available (shared-folder rows, regular rows, all rows).
110	    // The strict client re-checks deriveIpnsName(pubKey) === ipnsName, so deriving from
111	    // the name stays fail-closed.
112	    let pubKey = parsed.pubKey;
113	    if (!pubKey) {
114	      try {
115	        pubKey = Buffer.from(publicKeyFromIpnsName(cached.ipnsName)).toString('base64');
116	      } catch (error) {
117	        // A malformed / non-Ed25519 name yields no recoverable key → unverifiable record.
118	        // Return null → the caller 404s (fail closed).
119	        const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
120	        logger.warn(
121	          `Cached signed record for ${cached.ipnsName}: cannot recover pubKey from name (${message}) — discarding cached result`
122	        );
123	        return null;
124	      }
125	    }
126	    return { ...parsed, cid: cached.latestCid, sequenceNumber: cached.sequenceNumber, pubKey };
127	  } catch (error) {
128	    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
129	    logger.warn(`Failed to parse cached signed record for ${cached.ipnsName}: ${message}`);
130	    return null;
131	  }

## What I did

You were right that Test 15's direct DB access was a smell. I moved its coverage to where it belongs:

**Removed Test 15 from sdk-e2e** (`ipns-publish-gate.test.ts`):

- Updated the suite header to explain that TEE-05's seqFloor gate now lives in unit tests, and that the four remaining cases (16/17/TEE-07/20) stay because they genuinely need the live stack (real concurrency, the publish CAS, the tombstone round-trip).

- **unparseable cached `signedRecord` + no network** → fails closed (null)

`updateSharePermission(...)`, and `executeLazyRotation()` calls
`fetchPendingRotations()` / `updateShareKey()` / `completeShareRotation()`. As
written, exercising those flows is a guaranteed runtime crash, not just a
compile-time placeholder.

## Proposed fix (Phase 68, or a small interim guard now)

- Phase 68: wire the descriptor-ref rotation/grant path and remove the throws.
- Interim (if these UI paths are user-reachable before Phase 68): disable/hide
  the permission-change and lazy-rotation controls in `ShareDialog` and skip
  `executeLazyRotation()` so users cannot trigger the deferred throws, with a
  clear "coming soon"/disabled affordance. Do NOT convert the throws to silent
  no-ops — a no-op permission change would mislead the user into thinking access
  changed when it did not.

## Before doing this

Confirm whether the permission-downgrade and lazy-rotation entry points are
actually reachable in the current web build (routes/feature flags). If they are
already behind a disabled flag, this is purely a Phase 68 wiring task.

block CI — this is coverage-depth completeness only.

{
  "file_path": "/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.planning/todos/pending/2026-06-30-shares-bulk-revoke-direct-delete.md",
  "content": "---\ncreated: 2026-06-30T00:00:00.000Z\ntitle: Bulk-revoke shares with a direct DELETE instead of find + remove\narea: performance\nseverity: low\nfiles:\n  - apps/api/src/shares/shares.service.ts\n  - apps/api/src/shares/shares.service.spec.ts\n---\n\n> Deferred from the Phase 66 ship (CodeRabbit nitpick, Trivial). A perf-only\n> improvement on a non-hot path; switching the spec's shared query-builder mock to\n> sequence two execute() results is more churn than the gain warrants right now.\n> Verified SAFE to do (no behavior change) — see below.\n\n## Problem\n\n`SharesService.revokeForItems` (~line 170) loads full `Share` rows — including the\n`bytea` descriptor columns `readDescriptorRef` / `writeDescriptorRef` /\n`itemNameEncrypted` — into memory before deleting them:\n\n```ts\nconst shares = await manager.find(Share, {\n  where: { sharerId, rootIpnsName: In(uniqueNames) },\n});\nif (shares.length > 0) {\n  await manager.remove(shares);\n}\n// ...\nreturn { revokedShares: shares.length, revokedInvites: inviteResult.affected ?? 0 };\n```\n\nFor a subtree revoke touching many shares this needlessly fetches every blob.\n\n## Proposed fix\n\nUse a direct DELETE and its affected count:\n\n```ts\nconst shareResult = await manager\n  .createQueryBuilder()\n  .delete()\n  .from(Share)\n  .where('sharer_id = :sharerId', { sharerId })\n  .andWhere('root_ipns_name IN (:...names)', { names: uniqueNames })\n  .execute();\n// ...\nreturn { revokedShares: shareResult.affected ?? 0, revokedInvites: inviteResult.affected ?? 0 };\n```\n\n## Verified safe\n\nThe `Share` entity has NO `@OneToMany`, NO `@BeforeRemove`/`@AfterRemove` hooks,\nand NO `EntitySubscriber`; its only relations are owning-side `@ManyToOne` to\n`User` with `onDelete: 'CASCADE'` (a DB-level cascade that fires on USER deletion,\nnot on Share deletion). So `manager.remove()` triggers nothing that a raw DELETE\nskips — the change is behavior-preserving. If `In` becomes unused in\n`shares.service.ts`, drop it from the typeorm import.\n\n## Spec impact\n\n`shares.service.spec.ts` `revokeForItems` tests currently mock `manager.find` +\n`manager.remove` and assert `revokedShares` from `shares.length`. They must switch\nto the shared `queryBuilder` mock used for the invite UPDATE, sequencing\n`execute` with `mockResolvedValueOnce({ affected: <shares> })` then\n`mockResolvedValueOnce({ affected: <invites> })` (the share DELETE runs before the\ninvite UPDATE).\n"
}

Yes — now they are. That review (`pullrequestreview-4603705524`) bundled **7 body-level comments** (3 "Outside diff range" + 4 "Nitpick") *in addition* to the 19 inline threads I'd already resolved. They were posted on `e48a0cdc9`, so I verified each against current HEAD before acting — all 7 were still live. Disposition:

**Fixed now (4)** — in `191fd9ebd`:
| # | Comment | Fix |
|---|---------|-----|
| OD1 (Major) | republish sync can regress a newer IPNS record | Added a forward-only `sequence_number <= new` guard to `syncIpnsRecordSequence` — a stale TEE batch result can no longer overwrite a row a user publish already advanced |
| OD2 (Major) | `encryptedKey` allows odd-length hex (silent truncation) | Tightened to `/^(?:[0-9a-fA-F]{2})+$/`, matching the sibling descriptor-ref fields |
| NIT1 | invites spec: "already claimed/self-claim" test mocked the wrong exception | Now asserts `ConflictException` (what the service actually throws) |
| NIT4 | no test for the atomic single-claim race | Added a test: claim UPDATE affects 0 rows → `ConflictException` |

**Deferred (3)** — captured as todos, each with the reason:
- **OD3** (ShareDialog renders a fake "no recipients yet" empty state when the deferred fetch throws) → folded into the existing **Phase-68 web-stubs** todo; it's the same deferred-feature UI that needs gating.
- **NIT2** (bulk-revoke loads bytea blobs before deleting) → new perf todo. The verifier confirmed `Share` has no cascades/subscribers so a direct `DELETE` is safe, but it's a *Trivial* perf nitpick and forces a shared-mock rewrite for marginal gain.
- **NIT3** (shares.controller.spec uses non-contract-valid fixture strings) → folded into the shares-coverage todo; behavior-only test hygiene.

Why I deferred rather than fixed those three: OD3 is out-of-domain (web) and part of an intentional Phase-68 deferral; NIT2/NIT3 are trivial-severity and would churn passing specs for little benefit — exactly the "pre-existing / out-of-domain / trivial → todo" bucket.

## 2026-06-21 — Desktop E2E: tsx invocation + ESM/CJS + diagnostics-first debugging (CipherBox)

**Problem:** Desktop E2E (CI E2E Tests) was red whenever it actually ran. Two distinct, stacked failures hid behind a generic "did not verify after 24 attempts" message, and a multi-agent root-cause workflow mis-attributed the second one to a FUSE publish race.

**Lessons:**
- **`node node_modules/.bin/tsx <script>` is broken** — `.bin/tsx` is a POSIX shell shim, so node parses it as JS → `SyntaxError: missing ) after argument list`. To run a `.ts/.mts` from a Node child process, spawn `process.execPath` + `node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs <script>`, or `pnpm exec tsx`. This single line failed all 24 verify polls and looked like a data integrity / FUSE bug.
- **ESM-only deps + CJS-context tsx:** a `.ts` helper in a package without `"type":"module"` runs as CJS under tsx → `require()` of an ESM-only dep (`ipns@10`, whose `exports["."]` has no `require` condition) throws `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`. Fix: rename helper to `.mts` (forces ESM). Keep `.mts` in the typecheck `include` glob (`*.ts` does not match `.mts`).
- **Don't trust a multi-agent synthesis over the source.** The workflow confidently blamed a FUSE root-publish lost-update race (medium confidence on the interleaving). Reading the code refuted it (the mkdir snapshot is built via `build_folder_metadata` after the file is in `children`, so it's complete). The real cause was a swallowed child-process error. Verify deep-review "root causes" against current source before changing durability-critical code.
- **Diagnostics-first beats theory.** Surfacing the swallowed verify stdout/stderr on final failure revealed the exact error in ONE CI run, after days/cycles of mis-attribution. When a poll loop reports only "didn't succeed after N attempts," make it print the last child output before doing anything else.
- **Desktop E2E is dispatch-gated** — it SKIPS on main pushes that don't touch desktop paths, so a wall of green main runs can hide a broken desktop suite. Verify with `gh workflow run "CI E2E Tests" --ref <branch>`.
- **Commit-type discipline for release bumps:** test-infra-only fixes touching versioned package paths must be `chore(...)`, not `fix(...)`, or release-please bumps every touched package. Confirm via the PR's Release Preview ("No version bumps detected").

## 2026-06-24 — Triaging CodeRabbit durability findings: don't single-trace-dismiss (CipherBox, PR #553)

**Problem:** During /ship-phase 59, CodeRabbit's web review (which auto-fires on PR open + each push — no manual `@coderabbitai full review` needed) raised 5 threads including an inode.rs "Major" data-integrity finding. The local `coderabbit review --agent` CLI had surfaced the same finding, and I dismissed it as a false positive on a single code trace ("the encrypted hex gets unwrapped on re-resolution"). It was a **real durability bug**.

**Lessons:**
- **A durability/crypto defect usually sits two hops from the flagged line.** The flagged code set `file_ipns_private_key: None` on a pointer-swap rebuild; the bug only manifests because `resolve_file_pointer` later copies that None forward (without re-unwrapping the hex) AND both live per-file-publish consumers (`journal_helpers`→`read_ops` per-file IPNS publish gated on `Some`; cross-folder-move re-encrypt matched as `Some`) read the raw key directly from the inode field. A single trace from the flagged line missed all three hops.
- **Spawn an adversarial verifier per finding that follows the value to every consumer.** A 3-agent Workflow (one per Major finding, each grepping all consumers of the field and tracing publish/sign/re-encrypt sites) caught the real bug, correctly classified one as pre-existing (byte-identical to `main` → defer todo), and one as a false positive — with citations. My eyeball triage got the most important one wrong.
- **Verify CodeRabbit's *suggested fix* compiles before accepting.** Its replay.rs suggestion destructured `PublishResult::Conflict.current_sequence_number` (a `String`) into `record_publish`'s `u64` param — wouldn't compile. Good reason to dispute-as-false-positive, but only found by checking the type.
- **Triage rule that worked:** real+in-scope → fix now + regression test; correct-but-pre-existing (same on `main`, and self-healing e.g. CAS-gated) → defer todo, don't expand phase scope; suggested-fix-broken/unreachable/benign → dispute with evidence. Reply + `resolveReviewThread` each; re-query `reviewThreads` after to confirm `unresolved=0` and exactly 2 comments/thread (no dup replies).
- **Bleeding-edge local clippy ≠ CI clippy.** Local rust-1.91.0 flagged 24 pre-existing `too_many_arguments`/`same_item_push` lints in fuse/crypto that CI's (unpinned, older) toolchain accepts. Don't "fix" them. Instead run `cargo clippy -p <crate> --no-deps -- -D warnings`, extract the `-->` file:lines, and confirm none land on your changed lines — that's the real signal that your diff is lint-clean.

It was remediated during the ship review (presence-derived write authority), moving the register to 17/17 closed.\n\n**Context:** The threat register was authored at plan time and verified in verify-mitigations mode; SECURED status required a ship-time commit.\n**Source:** 66-SECURITY.md\n\n---\n\n### An orphan DTO survived the cutover\n\n`apps/api/src/shares/dto/update-encrypted-key.dto.ts` remains in the tree but is referenced by no controller or service.\n\n**Context:** Found in the verification anti-pattern scan; classified non-blocking since no route or service calls it.\n**Source:** 66-VERIFICATION.md\n\n---\n\n### Test 15 was narrowed to an unparseable-signedRecord case\n\nTest 15 Part B exercises garbage `signed_record` bytes (parseCachedRecord throws -> null, no network fallback) rather than the exact CID-mismatch (404) case the plan specified; the seqFloor below/at-floor split (Part A) is fully tested.\n\n**Context:** Documented as a Known Stub deviation from the plan's behavior spec.\n**Source:** 66-09-SUMMARY.md\n\n---\n\n## Patterns\n\n### TypeORM atomic conditional UPDATE as CAS\n\nExpress a compare-and-swap as a single `createQueryBuilder().update(Entity).set({...}).where(<fused predicates>)` (including a raw SQL literal such as `sequence_number + 1`), then branch on `result.affected`: `=== 1` success, `=== 0` do exactly one follow-up read to disambiguate the failure reason. No in-memory pre-check.\n\n**When to use:** When multiple clients race to publish/mutate the same row and you need exactly-one-winner semantics with no lost updates, folding several guards (sequence CAS, forward-only generation, tombstone null-check) into one statement.\n**Source:** 66-02-SUMMARY.md, 66-09-SUMMARY.md, 66-VERIFICATION.md\n\n---\n\n### Discriminated-union cache record with an explicit-absence floor\n\nModel a parsed cached record as `Fields | { seqFloor } | null`; the partially-populated case carries an explicit `{ seqFloor }` discriminant. Callers narrow via `'seqFloor' in r` and apply a forward-only floor comparison, failing closed on a below-floor or mismatched record.\n\n**When to use:** When a cached/derived row may legitimately lack the full signed payload but must still gate downstream serving safely instead of silently serving ungated data.\n**Source:** 66-02-SUMMARY.md, 66-VERIFICATION.md\n\n---\n\n### Stored-value fallback for optional CAS parameters\n\nCompute `effective = providedValue ?? storedRow.value` (per field) so an omitted optional parameter does not bind SQL NULL into a WHERE predicate (always false), keeping the atomic CAS valid for legacy unconditional callers.\n\n**When to use:** When adding a conditional UPDATE behind an API that still has callers who omit the conditional fields.\n**Source:** 66-02-SUMMARY.md\n\n---\n\n### Typed 410 via HttpException(GONE) as an OpenAPI marker\n\nThrow `HttpException({ error: 'IPNS_TOMBSTONED', ipnsName }, HttpStatus.GONE)` and add `@ApiResponse({ status: 410, schema })` on both the publish and resolve handlers so the typed marker body flows through `api:generate` into the SDK.\n\n**When to use:** When a terminal state (e.g. tombstone) must be a distinct, machine-readable status separate from a transient 409 conflict.\n**Source:** 66-02-SUMMARY.md\n\n---\n\n### Derivable-value recovery instead of a nullable persisted column\n\nDrop a nullable persisted value that has become a correctness footgun and recover it deterministically on demand (here: the Ed25519 key from the k51 IPNS name via `publicKeyFromIpnsName`) as the single recovery path.\n\n**When to use:** When a derivable value is stored nullable and the nullable column causes correctness/security bugs (e.g. null for shared rows).\n**Source:** 66-01-SUMMARY.md\n\n---\n\n### Descriptor-ref grant with capability-by-presence\n\nPersist a grant as `readDescriptorRef` (required) + optional `writeDescriptorRef` (presence encodes write capability) + root identity, with a plain `UNIQUE(sharer, recipient, root)` and hard-delete on revoke — no permission enum, no `revoked_at`, no per-key-type fan-out rows.\n\n**When to use:** When replacing per-key/per-permission grant rows with a single zero-knowledge wrapped-key residue where revocation is a hard delete.\n**Source:** 66-03-SUMMARY.md, 66-04-SUMMARY.md, 66-SECURITY.md\n\n---\n\n### Presence-derived authority from a server-trusted record\n\nDerive a capability (e.g. write access) from a field on the server-side invite/grant the user cannot forge — never from the request DTO the claimer supplies.\n\n**When to use:** In claim/redeem/grant-minting flows where the caller could otherwise self-escalate by populating a privilege field in their request body.\n**Source:** 66-SECURITY.md\n\n---\n\n### Atomic single-claim invite mint\n\nInside the atomic-claim transaction, after the single-claim UPDATE succeeds, mint exactly one `Share` via `manager.create(Share, {...})` copying the root identity from the invite row.\n\n**When to use:** When an invite must produce exactly one grant and the operation must be race-safe against concurrent claims.\n**Source:** 66-04-PLAN.md\n\n---\n\n### Drop-recreate TypeORM migration with greenfield waiver\n\nUse `MigrationInterface` with raw `queryRunner.query` DDL: `DROP TABLE ... CASCADE` then `CREATE TABLE` in dependency order, issue FK and index statements separately after each CREATE, and make `down()` throw when there is no rollback target.\n\n**When to use:** Greenfield/staging-only schema cutovers where reversibility is waived and column sets are authored directly from reshaped entities.\n**Source:** 66-05-SUMMARY.md\n\n---\n\n### Regenerated-client staging gate\n\nRun `pnpm api:generate` inside the worktree, stage `openapi.json` + `src/generated/` + `src/models/` together, and rely on `scripts/check-api-client.sh` (pre-commit) to require the regenerated files staged alongside API changes.\n\n**When to use:** Any API surface change in this monorepo, to stop a stale generated client masking a contract change (T-66-T6) and to keep the regen from leaking into the orchestrator tree.\n**Source:** 66-06-PLAN.md, 66-SECURITY.md\n\n---\n\n### compile-gate-stub (deferral throw)\n\nReplace a not-yet-implemented function body with `throw new Error('deferred to Phase N ...')` while keeping the exported signature so downstream consumers still typecheck; delete dead imports of removed dependencies to satisfy `noUnusedLocals`.\n\n**When to use:** After a breaking api-client/schema regeneration when the real consumer rework is deferred to a later phase but the monorepo typecheck gate must stay green and fail loudly at runtime.\n**Source:** 66-08-SUMMARY.md, 66-VERIFICATION.md\n\n---\n\n### Optional-param forwarding\n\nAdd a new optional parameter and thread it through every call layer (including retry attempts), defaulting to prior behavior when the param is absent.\n\n**When to use:** Extending a primitive to support a new server-side feature (e.g. a generation gate) without breaking or recompiling existing callers.\n**Source:** 66-07-SUMMARY.md\n\n---\n\n### Promise.allSettled concurrent-CAS race forcing (e2e)\n\nCapture a single `expectedSequenceNumber` and fire two concurrent publishes with it via `Promise.allSettled`, asserting exactly one fulfilled (200) and one rejected (409) with zero lost updates.\n\n**When to use:** Deterministically forcing a concurrent-publish race through the real client to API path to prove atomic CAS behavior.\n**Source:** 66-09-SUMMARY.md\n\n---\n\n### psql/execSync e2e precondition seeding\n\nSeed DB state that no public API can create (e.g. null-signedRecord seqFloor rows) using `execSync`-driven psql against temp SQL files. Reserve this for genuine internal/edge-case preconditions — pure decision logic is better moved to unit tests (as the seqFloor gate later was).\n\n**When to use:** Live-stack e2e tests that need internal rows as preconditions that the API itself will not produce.\n**Source:** 66-09-SUMMARY.md\n\n---\n\n### Caller-owns-key zeroization contract\n\nThe publish primitive must not zero the caller-supplied `ipnsPrivateKey`; key lifecycle and zeroization are owned by the caller.\n\n**When to use:** Designing crypto primitives where the key material is provided and managed by the caller rather than the primitive (zero only at the terminal owner).\n**Source:** 66-07-PLAN.md\n\n---\n\n## Surprises\n\n### A class-name substring grep also matched semantically-distinct method names\n\nThe acceptance criterion grepped for `FolderIpns` across non-spec source, which also matched `getFolderIpns`/`getAllFolderIpns` and `upsertFolderIpns`/`syncFolderIpnsSequence` — all had to be renamed (`getIpnsRecord`, `getAllIpnsRecords`, ...) along with their spec mocks and `describe()` blocks.\n\n**Impact:** Expanded a mechanical class/path rename into a public-API method rename touching `ipns.service.spec.ts`, `ipns.integration.spec.ts`, and `ipns.security.spec.ts`.\n**Source:** 66-01-SUMMARY.md\n\n---\n\n### A SQL NULL comparison silently breaks a CAS WHERE clause\n\nWhen `expectedSequenceNumber` was undefined (legacy unconditional publish), binding NULL into `sequence_number = :expected` made the predicate always false, so the atomic UPDATE affected 0 rows and wrongly failed every such publish.\n\n**Impact:** Required the `effectiveExpected = expectedSequenceNumber ?? existing.sequenceNumber` fallback (and the same for generation) to preserve backward-compatible publishes.\n**Source:** 66-02-SUMMARY.md\n\n---\n\n### Zero SQL foreign keys reference folder_ipns\n\nResearch found no table holds a SQL FK to `folder_ipns`; `ipns_republish_schedule`, `vaults`, and `shares` reference the IPNS name only as a plain varchar column.\n\n**Impact:** The rename-by-drop-recreate to `ipns_records` required no dependent-FK drops and left those tables untouched, simplifying the migration.\n**Source:** 66-05-PLAN.md\n\n---\n\n### One api:generate run changed 109 files in a single commit\n\nThe single `api:generate` run for plan 66-06 produced 109 changed files in one commit, including three new models (`tombstoneIpnsDto`, `ipnsControllerPublishRecord410`, `ipnsControllerResolveRecord410`).\n\n**Impact:** A large generated diff lands as one commit; reviewers must trust the generator and the `check-api-client.sh` gate rather than reviewing each file.\n**Source:** 66-06-SUMMARY.md\n\n---\n\n### migration:run still reported a no-op even after deleting the duplicate row\n\nAfter removing the duplicate migrations row, `migration:run` continued to report no pending migrations (suspected TypeORM caching or a separate matching quirk).\n\n**Impact:** Forced applying the cutover DDL directly via psql in a `BEGIN ... COMMIT` transaction and manually inserting `INSERT INTO migrations VALUES (1750000000000, 'ApiSchemaCutover1750000000000')` to cut the live schema over and unblock the sdk-e2e proof.\n**Source:** 66-09-SUMMARY.md\n\n---\n\n### The generation field was already present in the regenerated client DTOs\n\n`PublishIpnsEntryDto` and `PublishIpnsDto` already carried the `generation` field from prior plans in the phase, so the sdk-core change required no schema change of its own.\n\n**Impact:** The client-side change was purely additive param-forwarding — no new endpoints, auth paths, or schema changes.\n**Source:** 66-07-SUMMARY.md\n\n---\n\n### A stale-expected renewal returns 409, not 410, and preserves latestCid\n\nA renewal at a stale expected sequence yields a 409 (conflict) rather than a 410 (tombstone), and the latest CID stays intact (sdk-e2e Test 17).\n\n**Impact:** Confirms the publish gate cleanly separates concurrent-conflict semantics from terminal-tombstone semantics, so a benign stale renewal never destroys or masquerades as a dead record.\n**Source:** 66-VERIFICATION.md\n"
}
```
